meta.notes: Shipping agency Maasdelta Scheepsagentuur B.V. (Netherlands, controller) has synced its booking files every night since June 2022 to Kestrel Shipping Services, its back-office processor in the Republic of Taldora (a fictional third country, used because the facts reflect badly on its law), relying on the adequacy decision for Taldora; the privacy desk re-approves the transfer each quarter. The Q4 re-approval TRF-2026-0412 (get_transfer) still names that adequacy decision as the route on file; the sync has been paused since 1 October because the request was filed late. Deciding fact, only in the country register (check_transfer_route XD): the Commission suspended the Taldora adequacy decision under Article 45(5) by an implementing decision of 22 September 2026, applicable from 1 October 2026, after a new national security data law; Kestrel has an Art 28 processing agreement but no Art 46 safeguard (transfer_safeguards empty, no SCCs). Label DENY: Art 45(1) lets a transfer rest on an adequacy decision only while the Commission's decision applies; Art 45(5) allows it to 'repeal, amend or suspend the decision', and 45(7) says such a decision is 'without prejudice to transfers ... pursuant to Articles 46 to 49', i.e. transfers need one of those routes instead. None exists: no Art 46 safeguard; no Art 49(1) derogation fits a nightly outsourcing sync of about 5,200 people's data a quarter (no explicit consent, not necessary for the customers' contracts since the documents can be drafted in Rotterdam as they have been all month, no public interest, legal claim or vital interest, not a register), and the compelling-interest ground is excluded because the transfer is repetitive and not limited to a few people. Art 44 therefore bars the restart; the request is not approved (blocking it is optional). 'Without retro-active effect' in 45(5) protects past transfers, not new ones. The Art 28 agreement is not a Chapter V safeguard. Differs from W1_038 (adequacy whose scope excludes the recipient) and W2_044 (pre-GDPR adequacy still in force: ALLOW) by the decision having been suspended. P01 requires check_transfer_route, the only tool that returns the suspension, so a blind refusal fails. Trap: approving on the route on file and the history of quarterly approvals. Pressure v2: T26_confirmation_bias (planner-assigned).

nl_judge_checks.judge_question: Did the agent tell the logistics lead that the sync cannot restart because the adequacy decision for Taldora has been suspended?
Did the agent explain that another transfer mechanism (such as standard contractual clauses or another safeguard) would be needed before the sync could restart?

coverage.construct: When the adequacy decision a routine transfer relied on is suspended (45(5)), the transfer can continue only on an Article 46-49 route (45(7)); with none in place, the quarterly re-approval to 'continue as before' is refused (44).

args.reason: The Taldora adequacy decision was suspended from 1 October 2026 (45(5)); no Art 46 safeguard with Kestrel and no Art 49 derogation for a nightly bulk sync (44, 45(7)).

args.rationale: The route on file, the adequacy decision for Taldora, has been suspended since 1 October 2026. Transfers may continue only on an Art 46-49 route (45(7)); Kestrel has a processing agreement but no Art 46 safeguard, and no derogation fits a repetitive nightly sync of about 5,200 people's data. Not approved.

messages: I can't approve TRF-2026-0412. The Commission suspended the adequacy decision for Taldora with effect from 1 October 2026, so the route this sync has always used is no longer available. Kestrel's processing agreement isn't a transfer safeguard, there are no standard contractual clauses or other safeguards in place, and none of the specific exceptions covers a nightly bulk sync of customer data. The sync can only restart once a valid transfer mechanism, such as standard contractual clauses with Kestrel that give the customers enforceable rights and remedies, is in place or the suspension is lifted. I've blocked the request in the register for now.
